entries.title: Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai: a survey from before the eruption
paragraphs: This dive follows Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha’apai’s landscape before the 15 January 2022 eruption: a shallow summit basin, an island connection and volcanic slopes falling into deeper water.
The volcano rises roughly 2 km from the surrounding seafloor. Before 2022, its central basin lay about 150–200 m below sea level. A cone built in 2014–2015 joined the two older rim islands.

The January 2022 eruption drove a plume about 58 km high, sent pressure waves around the world and generated a destructive tsunami. Repeat seafloor mapping shows that the caldera deepened to about 850 m and widened from roughly 4.5 km to 4.8 km.

facts.label: Edifice height
facts.value: ~2 km from seafloor to the islands

entries.title: The caldera floor, before 2022
paragraphs: The earlier caldera contained a broad central basin, about 150–200 m deep in detailed surveys. This terrain grid reads about 132 m at the scan point.
Multibeam mapping before and after the January 2022 eruption reveals how dramatically the basin changed. The later surveys found its deepest part around 850 m.

entries.title: The islands, joined
paragraphs: The 2014–2015 eruption built a tephra cone between Hunga Tonga and Hunga Ha’apai, joining the two older islands. Tephra is fragmented volcanic material thrown out during an eruption.
The January 2022 eruption removed much of this connection and left the islands smaller and separated.

facts.value: pre-2022: islands joined by a shallow saddle

entries.title: The volcanic rim slope
paragraphs: West of the shallow basin, volcanic terrain falls toward deeper water. The scan point is about 469 m deep, beyond the central basin’s 150–200 m floor.
The banded tuff scarp's gullies and talus show how fragmented volcanic rock can form a steep slope.

entries.title: The outer flank of a 2-km volcano
paragraphs: Beyond the caldera rim, the seafloor drops away down the outer flank of the wider volcanic edifice -- this tile reads roughly 1,029 m deep here. The whole structure, from this outer base to the summit islands, rises about 2 km from the surrounding seafloor, making Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai one of the larger submarine volcanoes in the Tonga-Kermadec arc.
The flank is part of the wider volcanic edifice. The 2022 eruption also scoured slopes outside the caldera through fast-moving volcanic sediment flows.
